transcript.text: Good morning, Dr. Morgan. Thank you for the opportunity to restate my findings. My project roster review has identified a critical constraint: exactly eight students on the proposed roster of 20 have completed the district's media-ethics training. Those eight students are J1, J3, J6, J8, J11, J14, J17, and J20. Only those eight students are eligible to conduct recorded interviews. The remaining 12 students have not completed the required training and therefore may not conduct recorded interviews under district policy. Additionally, the approval file must include a training-verification record documenting this before the project can be approved. This means the draft plan's call for 20 student interviewers would need to be reduced to eight trained interviewers, or additional students would need to complete the media-ethics training before participating.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'd like to share my findings from the family-consent review now. My review has identified a critical issue with the plan's call for publishing all recordings on the public school website. Specifically, interviewees I2, I5, I9, I14, and I18 have not granted permission for public web publication. Their recordings may be used only in the school's internal archive, not on the public website. The plan must include a consent-exclusion record documenting this restriction before the project can be approved. This means the draft plan's blanket approach to publishing all recordings publicly is not permissible -- at least five recordings must be excluded from web publication and retained only internally.

transcript.text: Thank you, Dr. Morgan. I'd like to share my findings from the technology review now. My review has identified several critical issues with the draft plan's technology provisions. First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets instead. Second, all source files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive -- not on personal devices or general storage. Third, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation; indefinite retention as proposed in the draft plan is not permissible. I should note that storing source files in the restricted OralHistory drive does not prohibit publishing consented recordings on the public school website, so this requirement is compatible with the publication plan subject to the consent restrictions Mr. Lewis identified. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting these configurations before the project can be approved. In summary, the draft plan needs to be revised to replace personal phones with district tablets, use the restricted OralHistory drive for source file storage, implement a 45-day deletion timeline, and include the required secure-storage configuration record.
